// diagnostic E1017

Jet.InlineAlwaysReadsTrace

`#Inline(Always) fn` reads `context.trace`, which names the reading function's own frame

What

`#Inline(Always) fn` reads `context.trace`, which names the reading function's own frame

Why

`#Inline(Always)` guarantees every direct call is inlined on every tier, and `context.trace` starts at the frame of the function that reads it, while an inlined copy runs in its caller's frame. Sema refuses each mark that can't keep the guarantee: a call of itself or a cycle of marked calls (Jet.RecursiveInlineAlways), a use as a value (Jet.InlineAlwaysAddressTaken), a body over the size ceiling (Jet.InlineAlwaysTooLarge), `#Scrub` (Jet.InlineAlwaysScrub), a read of `context.trace` (Jet.InlineAlwaysReadsTrace) and a foreign body (Jet.InlineAlwaysForeign)

Fix

Drop `#Inline(Always)`, or read `context.trace` in the function's caller.

Worked example

First UI snapshot mentioning Jet.InlineAlwaysReadsTrace: Tests/UI/inline_always_reads_trace.stderr.

Error: Jet.InlineAlwaysReadsTrace: `depth` reads `context.trace`, so `#Inline(Always)` cannot expand it
  --> Tests/UI/inline_always_reads_trace.jet:3:46
    |
  3 | #Inline(Always) depth: fn() -> Int { context.trace.len() }
    |                                              ^^^^^
 Why: `context.trace` starts at the reading function's own frame, and an inlined copy has no frame of its own: the trace would name the caller instead. `#Inline(Always)` guarantees that every direct call is inlined on every tier, or the program is refused: sema refuses a function that calls itself or closes a cycle of marked calls (Jet.RecursiveInlineAlways), one used as a value (Jet.InlineAlwaysAddressTaken), one over the size ceiling (Jet.InlineAlwaysTooLarge), a `#Scrub` routine (Jet.InlineAlwaysScrub), one that reads `context.trace` (Jet.InlineAlwaysReadsTrace) and one with a foreign body (Jet.InlineAlwaysForeign).
 Fix: Drop `#Inline(Always)`, or read `context.trace` in the function that calls `depth`.
